A management text says that when performance misses objectives, the manager must "develop new actions to try to meet the objectives or report to higher-level managers that the objectives cannot be met
A practice guide titled "Limit Work in Progress" describes people taking on new tasks, "especially when a task they work on is waiting on external input."
It says the result is that "the person gets overloaded, nobody knows how the progress is, and tasks get stuck in a progressed state where nobody else can help."

A business text says gain-sharing plans encourage employees "to increase productivity within their specific work area regardless of the overall profit picture for the organization as a whole"
An accounting text concludes that "it is important that the performance management system not promote decisions that only benefit the manager to the detriment of the corporation."
The business text says "Successful businesses recognize that quality and productivity must go hand in hand."
It also says "It takes more than just inspecting goods at the end of the assembly line to ensure quality control."
The practice guide says "Without automated tests, queues form in front of testers."

It says "psychological safety of all participants is the key to getting trustworthy results out of a Postmortem"
A Department of Energy handbook describes "A traditional view of events and accidents is that they are caused by shortcomings in human competence, attention, or attitude."
The guide's case for limiting work in progress is that the person "stays responsive, flexible and the status stays visible."

The value-stream guide says focusing on the bottleneck "prevents efforts that make conditions worse by overloading an already constrained activity, and avoids distraction and excess work in progress."
The organizational behavior text says an incentive plan "should be as closely tied to actual job performance as possible"

The notebook describes a failure where "a team generates a solution and begins development right away without considering whether a solution is a good one."

sentences.missing: The cited account (lines 22174–22178) describes projects switching to CI but does not identify those projects as open-source. The open-source qualifier is explicit only for the different study of ignored build failures immediately afterwards.

sentences.claim: It reports another study finding that "12% of passing builds contained an actively ignored failure."

The value-stream guide says "If we don't focus, we likely achieve nothing" and asks the team to agree on one constraint before acting
the business text says bonuses "are replacing the raise as the way companies compensate employees for a job well done"
The organizational behavior text reproduces 1987 survey data in which 73 percent of companies reported success with individual incentives and 75 percent with small-group incentives
the business text reports that at Google "the large range in values for the award created jealousy instead of fostering better teamwork"
The iteration-planning guide says "Teams tend to focus on goals and activities more, when an end-date (deadline) has been set."
On speed, an entrepreneurship source says "The self-regulating problem solvers' biggest competitive advantage is the speed with which they recognize and provide solutions to problems."
The quality-first argument in the business text credits W. Edwards Deming
The software text pushes back, noting that "Software manufacturing involves copying patterns of bits, and perfect copies are easily made."
sentences.missing: The quoted observation about perfect bit copies is present, but the source does not establish the claimed pushback against the preceding company-wide, quality-first argument credited to Deming. Its discussion concerns hardware replication techniques; the converted text even says these solve a problem relevant to software production (lines 22923–22928).

sentences.claim: The business text says poor quality "usually results in lost sales."
The software text cites an Android study finding only "a slightly smaller average user rating in the Google Play Store" for apps using more fault-prone libraries
The postmortem guide asks reviewers to respect "the information that was available at the point of time the action happened" while also using hindsight to choose better paths
It also asserts "Psychological safety is the most important factor in high performing teams."
sentences.missing: The assertion is in the collection’s Measuring Psychological Safety article (lines 3923–3924), not the Blameless Postmortem guide to which “It also asserts” refers. The proposition is present, but its attribution to that guide is unsupported.

note: All 36 cited sentences were checked against searched regions of their cited converted sources. Uncited inferences are excluded; secondary mentions of Deming and Google are correctly sourced to the reporting text and are not wrong-book citations.
